skill.name: nature-figure
skill.description: Guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Nature-style scientific figure planning, backend selection, plotting, export, and QA for Python or R workflows.
skill.summary: Plan, build, and audit publication-ready scientific figures in Python or R.
skill.author: Community contribution, refactored into static/dynamic layers

security_audit.summary: Manual adjudication found no evidence of malicious intent or prompt injection in the reviewed files. The static findings are false positives from expected plotting output directories, Markdown formatting, dictionary key iteration, relative documentation links, and bundled preview media. The skill is still asset-heavy, so future releases should keep demo media minimal and review binary previews before publishing.

remediation.issue: Bundled binary preview assets increase the review surface.
remediation.suggestion: Keep only necessary PNG or PDF previews, document their source, and regenerate them from scripts when possible.

remediation.issue: Demo scripts create local output directories.
remediation.suggestion: Keep writes scoped to explicit figure output folders and avoid accepting unchecked traversal paths in future examples.

remediation.issue: Reference docs contain parent-relative asset links that trigger path heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer clearer repository-local documentation links or add notes that paths are internal reference assets only.

content.value_statement: Scientific figures often fail because story, evidence, export, and review checks are separated. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through one publication-ready workflow.
actual_capabilities: Requires a Python or R backend choice before generating figure code.
Builds a figure contract with conclusion, evidence hierarchy, panel map, export target, and review risks.
Provides Python guidance for matplotlib, seaborn, subplot_mosaic, editable SVG, and raster previews.
Provides R guidance for ggplot2, patchwork, ComplexHeatmap, svglite, cairo_pdf, and ragg exports.
Includes reference demos and chart atlases for multi-panel scientific figure layouts.
Runs QA checks for source data traceability, typography, color, statistics, and export formats.
limitations: It does not replace scientific judgment, statistical review, or journal editorial requirements.
It requires the user to supply real data, labels, units, and the target figure claim.
It does not support dashboards or Illustrator-first infographics.
It should not expose private template paths or internal reference filenames in final user output.

use_cases.title: Plan a manuscript figure
use_cases.description: Turn a research claim into a panel map, evidence hierarchy, export plan, and review checklist.

use_cases.title: Revise a submitted figure
use_cases.description: Audit typography, statistics, color, source data notes, and journal-ready output formats before resubmission.

use_cases.title: Build method comparison panels
use_cases.description: Adapt bundled scientific chart patterns into clean comparison figures using real project data.

prompt_templates.title: Start a figure plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning before any plotting code exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nature-figure. I need a Python or R manuscript figure. The main conclusion is [claim]. The data columns are [columns]. Plan the figure before writing code.

prompt_templates.title: Generate backend-specific figure code
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a first implementation after the backend is chosen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nature-figure with Python. Build a multi-panel figure from my dataframe with panels [panel list]. Export editable SVG and a PNG preview.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an existing figure
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a draft figure for publication risks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nature-figure with R. Review my current figure for readability, statistical labeling, color, typography, source-data traceability, and export quality. Return prioritized fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a demo into a submission figure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced adaptation of a bundled visual pattern.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nature-figure with Python. Adapt the closest bundled demo pattern to my real data and manuscript claim. Do not reuse demo labels or reveal internal paths.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for a Python figure showing tumor response, histology, and safety markers.
output: A figure contract that states the core claim and evidence order.
A panel plan with a dominant efficacy panel and supporting safety panels.
A Python plotting workflow with editable vector export and source-data notes.

output_examples.input: A student shares an R heatmap figure and asks why it looks crowded.
output: A prioritized review of typography, annotation density, color scale, and legend placement.
Concrete revision steps for patchwork or ComplexHeatmap output.
A final export checklist for SVG, PDF, TIFF, and preview files.

output_examples.input: A team wants a Nature-style method comparison figure from existing benchmark tables.
output_examples.output: A backend-gated plan with comparison bars, interval plots, statistical labels, export settings, and checks against misleading visual emphasis.

best_practices: Choose Python or R first and keep the backend exclusive for plotting, previewing, and QA.
Define the core conclusion and evidence chain before drawing panels.
Export editable SVG or PDF plus a raster preview, and verify source-data traceability.
anti_patterns: Generating mock data when the user has not chosen a backend or supplied a clear target.
Mixing Python and R outputs in one figure workflow without user approval.
Copying demo labels, private paths, or internal asset names into user-facing deliverables.

faq.question: Does this skill make figures automatically?
faq.answer: It guides planning, code generation, export, and QA. The user still provides data, claims, and review context.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Why does it ask Python or R first?
faq.answer: The workflow keeps one plotting backend active, so code, preview, export, and QA stay consistent.

faq.question: Does it only support Nature journals?
faq.answer: No. It targets Nature-style and high-impact manuscript figures, but the same checks help many journals.

faq.question: Can it revise an existing figure?
faq.answer: Yes. It can audit layout, typography, color, statistics, source-data notes, and export formats.

faq.question: Does it create dashboards?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on static manuscript figures, not dashboards or product analytics interfaces.
